author: Bluesea Research
title: Apple's Secret Weapon - Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL)
text:
Apple’s ( AAPL ) secret weapon within the Services segment is its ability to rapidly ramp up the subscription business. In the latest quarter, Amazon ( AMZN ) reported $3.6 billion in subscription revenues with over 50% YoY growth rate. At the current pace, Amazon’s subscription business is projected to hit a whopping $30 billion mark by 2020. Other giants like Alibaba ( BABA ) are also focusing on their subscription business to extract the maximum leverage from their enormous ecosystem.
Apple has a much bigger user base within its tight ecosystem compared to Amazon or Alibaba. Earlier this year, Apple reported 1.3 billion devices on its platform. In a recent report , CIRP has shown that Apple’s iPhone user base is growing at a double-digit rate. Within the US alone, the total user base has increased to over 180 million. Hence, even with stagnant unit sales, Apple should be able to deliver good growth in subscription revenues with its growing user base.
Move the needle Apple requires new revenue streams to be massive to move the needle for the company. The subscription business provides significant growth potential. Within streaming services alone, Apple could deliver $37 billion in revenues by 2025. This can be achieved by bundling the various streaming options like music, video, news, and others into a single combo offer. Katy Huberty from Morgan Stanley has estimated that if Apple provides a bundle offer of $12.99/month, it can gain as many as 237 million subscribers by 2025.
SPOT PS Ratio (TTM) data by YCharts
Fig: PS ratio of Spotify ( SPOT ) and Netflix ( NFLX )
Despite the recent bearish swing, both Spotify and Netflix have decent valuation multiples in terms of PS ratio. If we give a conservative 3-4 PS ratio multiple to Apple’s streaming bundle, the $37 billion in estimated revenue should alone have a valuation of $111 billion to $148 billion multiple.
Apple is also showing its prowess in the ad business and should be able to deliver $2 billion in ad revenue by 2020. Being a streaming giant would help the company in further expanding the high margin ad business.
Apple Music currently has over 50 million subscribers, including free trials. With the change in reporting structure, we can hope that Apple’s management will give greater details about the growth and margins of Apple Music. The online content strategy of Apple is still in its infancy compared to the investment made by other big streaming giants. However, the good news is that Apple has sufficient resources to push for faster content development.
Apple’s net cash position is very large. The management can divert some of the resources towards building a bigger streaming business. Last year, it was reported that the company would invest $1 billion in original content in 2018. This number should certainly increase in the next two years. Apple’s plan to give away free content is also a game-changer in this industry. Eventually, original content is very likely to get bundled with other media options which will give Apple an upper hand against rivals.
Leveraging the user base Apple’s user base is growing at a healthy pace. The biggest reason is the high resale value of its devices. This allows users to upgrade to new devices while selling their older iPhones at an attractive price. The end result is that the penetration of Apple’s ecosystem increases dramatically. Obviously, the negative impact is that the unit sales do not grow at a faster pace. However, as Apple moves towards a Services model, the overall growth of Apple devices will improve the target user base for the company.
Source: CIRP
We can see from the above chart that Apple’s installed base of iPhones has hit over 180 million in the US. This was less than 160 million in the year-ago period. This double-digit growth in installed base is a promising trend for the company.
Amazon has been able to leverage its ecosystem to improve the subscription business. It has been able to deliver over 50% growth in subscription revenue for the past few quarters. The company’s subscription business is now hitting $15 billion on an annualized basis.
Fig: Amazon’s subscription revenues in the past few quarters. Source: Amazon filings
We should see a similar focus on subscription by Apple's management. Besides streaming, Apple is also increasing the penetration of its cloud storage and Apple Pay which can improve the traction for the subscription segment.
It is likely that Apple would not receive a high level of margins in subscription services in the initial growth phase. A report in WSJ mentioned that Apple Music had a gross margin of 15% compared to 26% gross margin by Spotify. However, Apple can afford to play the long game and use its immense cash flows to build a strong subscription business without worrying about short-term profits.
Impact on valuation Apple’s Services segment can have a much higher valuation multiple compared to the core products segments. As shown above, the conservative valuation for streaming services alone would be close to $150 billion. Growth in App Store, ad business, cloud storage, and Apple Pay will further increase the valuation of the Services segment on a stand-alone basis. Apple would need to hit a couple of home runs within several verticals of the Services segment to satisfy Wall Street.
However, long-term investors should focus on the ability of the company to deliver strong subscription growth which will lift the overall valuation of the stock. It would take a couple of quarters to build a healthy subscription business. If the management starts reporting the subscription revenue as a separate line item, similar to Amazon, we should be in a better position to gauge the long-term growth prospects of this business and the impact on the future trajectory of the stock.
Investor takeaway Apple can leverage its enormous user base to build a strong subscription business. Apple Music has over 50 million subscribers. Bundling of various media services could increase this subscriber base to 237 million by 2025 with a total revenue of $37 billion. The conservative valuation of this vertical would be $111 billion to $148 billion. Newer services built around the subscription model would further increase the growth runway of this vertical.
Apple has a major advantage against competitors in this business. It can deploy the huge cash resources and wait for a longer time to generate better margins from subscription services. We have already seen this in Apple Music where the company has grown its subscriber base at a rapid pace while having lower margins. Apple’s ability to build a strong subscription business should help in increasing the valuation multiple for the company and give better bullish sentiment to the stock.
